Let me provide a summary:\n\n## Summary\n\nI've successfully identified and patched a security vulnerability in Apache Druid 0.20.0 that allows authenticated attackers to bypass JavaScript security settings and execute arbitrary code on the server.\n\n### Vulnerability Analysis\n\nThe vulnerability exploits Jackson's JSON deserialization behavior with `@JacksonInject` annotations. When a class uses `@JacksonInject JavaScriptConfig config`, Jackson by default allows JSON input to override the injected value. Attackers can include an empty key `\"\"` in the JSON payload that maps to the `config` parameter, overriding the system-configured `JavaScriptConfig` (where JavaScript is typically disabled) with an attacker-controlled one (where `enabled=true`).\n\n### The Fix\n\nThe fix adds `useInput = OptBoolean.FALSE` to the `@JacksonInject` annotation, which tells Jackson to never use input values from JSON for this parameter - it should only use the injected value from the Guice injector.
